source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And it came to pass from that [time] onward, Yeshua went about through the towns and fortified places [or: villages], seeking out [the people] and proclaiming the kingdom of YHWH, and with him were the twelve disciples.

translation_notes: ומגיד: The consonants מגיד could relate to H1517 'tendon/thong', but contextually this is the hiphil participle of נגד 'to declare/tell'. The candidate H1517 (גיד = tendon) shares some consonants but makes no sense next to 'kingdom of YHWH'. This is clearly מַגִּיד, 'one who declares'.
מלכות: Candidates H4438 'kingdom/dominion' vs H3575 'Cuth, a province of Assyria'. In context paired with YHWH, 'kingdom' is the coherent reading.

עשר: Candidates include H6235 'ten', H6240 '-teen (in combination)', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth'. Since ה'נים (the damaged numeral) + עשר = 'twelve' and this modifies 'disciples', H6240 (combination numeral) is best, reading שנים עשר = twelve.
יהוה: H3068 and H3069 are the same divine name. Chose H3068 as the primary entry.
textual_notes: מ'ם and ה'נים contain damaged/abbreviated characters (marked with apostrophe). מ'ם likely reads משם ('from there/then') or a similar temporal phrase. ה'נים likely reads השנים ('the two') which combines with עשר to form 'twelve'.
ובמגדלים could mean 'in towers/fortresses' or by extension 'in large/fortified towns'. The word מגדל means tower but is also the root of place names like Magdala.

verses.literal: And it was done from then and onward Yeshua walking in towns and in towers seeking and declaring [the] kingdom [of] YHWH and there were with him the twelve disciples

verses.translation: And certain women who had been healed from evil spirit[s] and other ailments — including Miriam of Magdala [the Magdalite], from whom he had driven out seven demons —

translation_notes: מרוח: Candidates include H4790 'bruised/emasculated' and H7307 'wind/breath/spirit'. With the preposition מ- ('from'), followed by רעה ('evil'), 'from evil spirit' makes perfect contextual sense — women healed from evil spirits. H4790 'emasculated' is nonsensical for women.

רעה: Candidates H7462 'to shepherd/tend', H7463 'male companion', H7464 'female associate', H7465 'breakage/evil'. As an adjective modifying רוח ('spirit'), H7465 'evil/bad' produces the coherent image 'evil spirit'. A shepherding spirit or companion spirit is forced.

ושאר: Candidates H7603 'yeast', H7604 'to swell up/be redundant', H7605 'remainder', H7607 'flesh/food'. Following a list of ailments and preceding ח6ליים ('illnesses'), H7605 'remainder/other' is the natural reading: 'and other illnesses'.
שבעה: Candidates H7653/H7654 'satiety', H7655 'seven', H7656 'Shebah (a well)', H1158 'to gush/desire'. Before שדים ('demons'), 'seven demons' is the coherent reading.

שדים: The only Strong's candidate offered is H7708 'Siddim, a valley'. However, the consonants שדים clearly also support שֵׁדִים (demons, from שֵׁד H7700). In context — driven out from her seven ___ — 'demons' is the only coherent reading.

ממנה: Candidates include H4487 'to weigh out/appoint', H4488-4490 (measured amounts), H5089 'lamentation'. However, the plain morphological reading is מִמֶּנָּה 'from her' (preposition מן + 3fs suffix). This is a standard pronoun form, not a lexical entry. Context demands 'from her'.
textual_notes: ח6ליים contains a damaged character (marked '6'). The likely reading is חליים or חולים ('illnesses/sick ones').

שדים: The Strong's candidate provided (H7708, Siddim valley) does not fit. The consonants clearly support שֵׁדִים 'demons' (from H7700 שֵׁד), which is not listed among candidates but is the only coherent reading.

verses.literal: And some women who were healed from spirit evil and other illnesses and Miriam the Magdalite who he drove out from her seven demons

verses.translation: And Yochanah, wife of Kuzan, steward [or: estate-manager] of Herod, and Shoshannah, and the rest of many women who ministered to Yeshua from their own resources [possessions]. [Manuscript damage: fragmentary text follows with repeated verb forms and incomplete phrases] ... on account of ...

translation_notes: מורשה: H4181 'a possession'. In context — describing Kuzan's role relative to Herod — this likely indicates 'steward' or 'one in charge of possessions/estate' of Herod.
ושאר: Same as section 2: H7605 'remainder/rest of'. Before 'many women', this reads naturally as 'the rest of many women'.
כי: H3587 'a brand/scar' vs H3588 'because/for/that'. In a clause with לא, the conjunction H3588 is the natural reading.
בעבור: H5668 'on account of / in order that' vs H5669 'stored grain'. At the end of a clause, 'on account of' is the logical adverbial reading.
textual_notes: This section appears heavily damaged or corrupted. After מרשותן, there is a sequence of repeated verb forms (תהיו, יהיו, תהיינה) that do not form coherent syntax, along with single-letter fragments (ת, י). This strongly suggests scribal error, marginal glosses, or manuscript damage.
ש'רתו contains a damaged character. The likely reading is שרתו (שָׁרְתוּ) 'they served/ministered'.
שבשבילה is an unusual compound; it appears to be ש + בשביל + ה = 'that on account of her', but the surrounding damaged text makes the full clause unclear.
The entire latter half of this section (from לא onward) cannot be reliably translated due to apparent textual corruption.

verses.literal: And Yochanah wife [of] Kuzan steward [of] Herod and Shoshannah and rest [of] many women who served Yeshua from their possessions not ... because not to her ... ... ... ... ... ... and they drew near they trusted ... ... on account of

verses.translation: And many peoples assembled and came to him from the cities, and they pressed toward Yeshua [to hear him] speak a parable [or: figurative discourse]

translation_notes: מן (consonants מן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from (Aramaic)', H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from the cities' is the only coherent spatial reading.

למשול (consonants למשול): The root משל can mean H4910 'to rule', H4911 'to speak figuratively', or שול H7757 'skirt'. In context, followed by משל (a parable), H4911 'to speak in figurative language' produces the coherent image of speaking a parable.

משל (consonants משל): Candidates: H4910 'to rule', H4911 'to use figurative language', H4912 'a parable/maxim', H4913 'Mashal (place)', H4914 'a satire', H4915 'empire/parallel'. Chose H4912 because it serves as the noun object of the preceding infinitive 'to speak'.
לישוע (consonants ישוע): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua' (proper name), H3443 (same). Chose H3442 as a proper name in context — people came to a person named Yeshua.

וצערו: The consonants צער can relate to H6810 'small/young' or H6819 'to go out/march out'. In context of people coming from cities and pressing toward someone, H6819 in the sense of going forth/pressing toward fits the narrative of crowds moving toward Yeshua.
textual_notes: וצערו is uncertain: the root צער could mean 'to be small/insignificant' or 'to go out/march forth'. Another possibility is that it reflects a later Hebrew usage meaning 'they pressed/crowded'. The exact nuance is unclear from consonants alone.

verses.literal: And peoples many were gathered and came to him from the cities and went out to Yeshua to speak a parable

verses.translation: And he told them [this]: A sower went out sowing his seed, and while he was sowing, [some] fell from him onto the path and was trampled underfoot, and the birds of the sky [or: heavens] devoured it

translation_notes: שזרע (consonants ש+זרע): Candidates for זרע: H2232 'to sow', H2233 'seed', H2234 'posterity', H2235 'vegetable'. With the ש prefix (relative 'that/who'), H2232 'one who sows / a sower' fits as the subject of the clause.
נפל (consonants נפל): Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 (Aramaic same), H5309 'abortion/miscarriage'. Chose H5307 because seed falling to the ground is the coherent image.
לדרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/path'. Chose H1870 because the preposition ל + noun 'path' gives 'to/onto the path', which is where seed falls.

שמים (consonants שמים): Candidates: H8064 'sky/heavens', H4325 'water', H3220 'sea'. Chose H8064 because 'birds of the sky' is the natural collocation; 'birds of water' or 'birds of the sea' would be a different category of bird and doesn't fit the agricultural scene.
textual_notes: ואמרו could be parsed as 'and he said' (with the vav + 3ms) or 'and they said' (3mp). In context, since the parable is being told by one person (Yeshua), 'and he said' is more likely, though the consonants could support either.

verses.literal: And he said to them that a sower sowed his seed and while he [was] sowing [some] fell from him to the path and was trampled and birds of the sky ate it

verses.translation: And other seed fell from him upon the rocks, and when the seed sprouted [or: came forth], it withered because it had no moisture from the earth

translation_notes: וזרע (consonants זרע): Candidates: H2232 'to sow', H2233 'seed', H2234 'posterity', H2235 'vegetable'. Chose H2233 'seed' because it is the subject — 'and seed other fell'.

אחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'other/another', H313 'Acher'. Chose H312 'other' because 'other seed' parallels the parable structure of different portions of seed.
על (consonants על): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon', H5922 (Aramaic), H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 'upon' as a preposition — seed fell upon the rocks.
וכאשר (consonants כ+אשר): The אשר candidates include H834 'who/which/when'. With כ prefix and ו prefix, 'and when' is the standard conjunction for temporal clauses.
הזרע: Chose H2233 'seed' (with article ה) as the subject of 'went out / sprouted'.
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because 'there was not moisture' is the coherent reading.
textual_notes: נתיבש appears to be a hitpael or nitpael form of יבש (to dry up, H3001), not listed among candidates. The consonants נ-ת-י-ב-ש strongly suggest a reflexive/passive of יבש, 'it dried itself up / withered'.
לחות: Not among provided candidates. The consonants suggest לחות from the root לח (H3955 'moisture/freshness'). This reading fits perfectly in context.

verses.literal: And seed other fell from him upon the rocks and when the seed went out it dried up because not was to it moisture from the earth

verses.translation: And the other [seed] fell in the midst of thorns, and the thorns grew up together with the seed and choked it

translation_notes: והאחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H312 'other'. Chose H312 with the article ה — 'the other [seed]' continuing the parable's pattern.

עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 'with' because 'the thorns grew up with the seed' produces a coherent agricultural image; 'the thorns grew up [as] a people' does not.
הזרע (consonants זרע): Chose H2233 'seed' — the thorns grew alongside the seed.
textual_notes: וחנקשהו: The consonants suggest חנק (to choke/strangle) plus a pronominal suffix הו ('it'). The שׁ in the middle is unusual — it may be a relative particle ש fused in, or a scribal peculiarity. The meaning 'and choked it' is clear from context.

verses.literal: And the other fell in midst of thorns and the thorns went out with the seed and choked it

verses.translation: And the other seed fell in good earth and produced fruit a hundredfold, and as he said this he cried out: Whoever has ears, let him hear!

translation_notes: וזרע: Chose H2233 'seed' as the subject continuing the parable pattern.
האחר: Chose H312 'the other' with article — 'the other seed'.
כמאה (consonants מאה): Candidates: H3967 'a hundred', H3968 'Meah (tower)', H3969 'a hundred (Aramaic)'. Chose H3967 — 'like a hundred' makes sense with the following 'fold'.
וזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'and this [he was] saying' makes sense; 'and a sheep' does not fit.
אומר: The candidate H201 'Omar (proper name)' does not fit. The consonants אמר clearly map to the participle of H559 'to say' — 'saying/one who says'.
שיש (consonants ש+יש): Candidates: H7893 'marble/white', H3426 'there is/exists'. Chose ש (relative) + H3426 'there is' = 'who has / whoever has'. 'Whoever [is] marble' produces no coherent image.
textual_notes: כפלים: Not in provided candidates. The consonants כפל suggest H3718 'double/fold'. The ים suffix here likely intensifies — 'a full hundredfold' rather than 'hundred doubles (plural)'.

verses.literal: And seed the other fell in earth good and made fruit like a hundred fold and this saying he cried out whoever that has to him ears let him hear

verses.translation: And his disciples asked him: What manner of thing [or: word, matter] is this?

translation_notes: דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 'matter/word' because the disciples are asking what kind of word/teaching this is.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the copulative pronoun 'is' in a nominal sentence — 'what matter is this?'
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this' as a demonstrative pronoun.

verses.literal: And his disciples asked him what matter is this

verses.translation: And to them he said: To you it is given to know the kingdom of the heavens, but to others [it is given] in parables, so that even if they see they will not see, and even if they hear they will not hear [or: understand]

translation_notes: ולהם (consonants ל+הם): Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — ל+הם = 'to them', introducing the recipients of speech.
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 — 'he said' as the main verb of the clause.
מלכות: H4438 'kingdom/dominion' fits; H3575 'Cuth' is a place name that doesn't fit.
שמים: Candidates: H8064 'sky/heavens', H4325 'water', H3220 'sea'. Chose H8064 — 'kingdom of the heavens' is a coherent theological concept.

להכיר (consonants ל+ה+כיר): The candidate H3600 'cooking range' makes no sense. The consonants נכר/כיר with ה prefix more likely reflect the hiphil infinitive of נכר (H5234 'to recognize/know'). 'To know the kingdom' is coherent; 'to cooking-range the kingdom' is not.
אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H61 'but/yet/truly'. Chose H61 — 'but' as an adversative conjunction contrasting 'to you... but to others'.
משל: Candidates: H4910 'to rule', H4912 'a parable'. Chose H4912 — 'to others [in] a parable' continues the contrast.
בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — 'in order that' introduces a purpose clause.
שאם (consonants ש+אם): Candidates for אם: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. Chose ש (relative) + H518 'if' = 'that if'. 'That mother' makes no sense here.
ולא: H3808 'not' — simple negation.
textual_notes: להכיר: The only provided candidate is H3600 'cooking range', which is clearly wrong contextually. The consonants כיר with ל+ה prefix almost certainly represent the hiphil infinitive construct of נכר (H5234), 'to recognize/know'. This is a strong reading but relies on a root not listed among the provided candidates.

The repeated יראו could theoretically derive from ירא 'to fear' rather than ראה 'to see'. However, the parallel structure with ישמעו 'they hear' strongly favors ראה 'to see' — the pairing of seeing and hearing is the natural reading.

verses.literal: And to them he said to you [it] is given [the] kingdom of the sky to know but to others a parable because that if they see and not they see and if they hear not they hear

verses.translation: The meaning [or: matter, word] is this: the seed is the word of YHWH

translation_notes: הדבר (consonants ה+דבר): Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1697 'a word/matter'. Chose H1697 with the article — 'the matter/word'. A vizier does not fit the explanatory context of a parable.
הוא (first): H1931 'he/it' as copula — 'the matter is this'.
זה: H2088 'this' — demonstrative.
הזרע: H2233 'seed' with article — 'the seed'.
הוא (second): H1931 as copula — 'the seed is'.
דבר: H1697 'word' — 'word of YHWH'.
יהוה: H3068 'YHWH, the self-Existent'.

verses.literal: The matter is this the seed is [the] word of YHWH

verses.translation: That which fell near the path — they are those who hear it, and afterward the Adversary [Satan] comes and removes the word from their heart, so that they will not believe and will not be saved [or: delivered]

translation_notes: לדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'road/path'. Chose H1870 — 'near the path' is the coherent spatial reading.
והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'and they are those who hear'.
אחר: Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H312 'other'. Chose H310 — 'after thus' = 'afterward'.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'after thus' = 'afterward' is a standard Hebrew temporal phrase.
השטן: Candidates: H7853 'to accuse', H7854 'Satan/adversary'. Chose H7854 with the article — 'the Adversary/Satan' as a personified agent who removes the word.
הדבר: Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1697 'word/matter'. Chose H1697 — 'the word' that was sown, consistent with section 8.
בעבור: H5668 'in order that / on account of'. Purpose clause introducing the Adversary's intent.
שלא / ושלא: ש (relative) + H3808 'not' = 'that not / so that not'.
textual_notes: ש<ומעין: The angle bracket suggests a textual corruption or uncertain letter. The reading שומעין 'hearing/listeners' (plural participle, possibly with Aramaic-style plural ending ין-) is the most coherent reconstruction given the context of people who 'hear' the word.
מלבם: Not among listed candidates. Parsed as מ (from) + לב (H3820 'heart') + הם (their) = 'from their heart'. This is a straightforward reading.

verses.literal: That fell near to the path and they [are] those that hear it and comes after thus the Adversary and brings out the word from their heart in order that not they believe and that not they be saved

verses.translation: And the seed that fell upon the rock — they are those who receive the word of YHWH with joy, but these have no roots, because they existed [or: believed] only for a season, and in a time of testing [or: trial] they fall away [or: separate themselves]

translation_notes: והזרע: H2233 'seed' with article and vav — continuing the parable explanation.
על: Chose H5921 'upon' — seed fell upon the rock.
הסלע: Candidates: H5553 'craggy rock', H5554 'Sela (place)'. Chose H5553 — a rock surface where seed cannot take root.
הם: Chose H1992 'they' — identifying the seed with people.
שבשמחה: ש (relative) + ב (in) + H8057 'joy' = 'who in joy / with gladness'.
דבר: H1697 'word' — 'word of YHWH'.
ולאלו (consonants ו+ל+אלו): Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'if'. Neither fits well. More likely אלו is a demonstrative pronoun 'these' (related to אלה H428). Chose as 'and to these'.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/there is not', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'there are no roots'.
כי: H3588 'because' — introducing the reason.
לזמן: Candidates: H2163 'to fix a time', H2165 'an appointed occasion/season'. Chose H2165 — 'for a season/time', meaning their faith is temporary.

ובעת (consonants ו+ב+עת): Candidates: H1204 'to fear' (בעת as root), H6256 'time' (עת as root with ב prefix). Chose ב + H6256 'in a time of' — 'in a time of trial' is coherent; 'and to fear trial' would require different syntax.
נפרדים: From root פרד (H6504 'to separate/divide'). Niphal participle plural — 'they separate themselves / fall away'.
textual_notes: ולאלו: The provided candidates (H431 'lo!', H432 'if') do not match the apparent meaning well. The form likely represents a demonstrative 'these' (related to אלה), not listed among candidates. The contextual reading 'and to these [there are] no roots' is clear.

נסיון: Not among provided candidates with a Strong's number. The consonants suggest a noun from the root נסה (H5254 'to test/try'), yielding 'trial/testing'. This is the standard Hebrew noun for testing or temptation.

verses.literal: And the seed that fell upon the rock they [are] those that in joy receive [the] word of YHWH and to these there are no roots because for a time they were and in a time of trial they separate

verses.translation: And that seed which fell among the thorns — they are those who hear the word of YHWH, yet they have a heart [or: mind, inclination] and industriousness [directed] toward riches and toward the pleasures [or: delights] of this life. They are choked and do not bear [or: produce, carry] fruit.

translation_notes: זרע (ZR'): Candidates: H2232 'to sow', H2233 'seed', H2234 'posterity', H2235 'vegetables'. Chose H2233 because the passage describes something that fell into a location, which fits 'seed' as a noun rather than a verb or posterity.
הם (HM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because it functions as a pronoun identifying the subject ('they are those who...').
דבר (DBR): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because it pairs naturally with YHWH as 'the word of YHWH'.
להם (LHM): The consonants could be H3859 'to rankle' or the preposition ל + הם (H1992 'them'). Chose ל + H1992 because 'there is to them' (= they have) is standard Hebrew idiom with יש.

האלו (H'LW): Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if/nay'. In context this is the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (post-biblical Hebrew form), pointing to 'the life' — chose H431 as closest match for the demonstrative usage.
textual_notes: וחריצות is not attested in the Strong's candidates provided. The consonants חרצ suggest 'diligence, industriousness, sharpness' — but could also relate to 'decisiveness' or 'eagerness'. Context of being drawn to riches suggests 'diligence/eagerness [toward wealth]'.
נושאין could derive from נשא (to carry/bear) — 'bearing fruit' is a natural agricultural image. The participial form with ין ending is late/Mishnaic Hebrew.

verses.literal: And that seed that fell among thorns they [are] those that hear [the] word [of] YHWH and there is to them heart and diligence in riches and in pleasures of the life these they [are] choked and not bearing fruit

verses.translation: And whoever lights a lamp does not light it in order to hide it or to place it behind [something], but rather in order to set it upon the lampstand [or: chandelier] or upon a high place, so that those who enter into the house will see [the light].

translation_notes: בעבור ('BWR): Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because the context requires a purpose clause — 'in order that he hide it'.
רק (RQ): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because it introduces a contrast: not to hide it, but rather to place it on the lampstand.
על ('L): Candidates: H5920 'the top/aloft', H5921 'upon/over', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 because placing a lamp 'upon' the lampstand is the natural physical image.
מקום (MQWM): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing spot', H6965/H6966 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because it serves as a noun modified by 'high'.
בבית (BBYT): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'object marker'. Chose H1004 because entering 'the house' is the natural setting for seeing a lamp.

נר (NR): The only Strong's candidate is H5369 'Ner (proper name)'. However, the consonants נר universally denote 'lamp' in Hebrew (cf. related H5216). The context of lighting and placing on a lampstand demands 'lamp', not a personal name.
textual_notes: נר is listed only as H5369 (a proper name) in the candidates, but the consonants clearly mean 'lamp' in this context. The standard Strong's number for 'lamp' is H5216 (ניר/נר). The provided candidate list appears incomplete.

verses.literal: And who that lights a lamp not is lighting it in order that he hide it or place it behind only in order that he set it upon the lampstand or upon a place high in order [that] those that enter into the house will be seeing

verses.translation: For no thing [or: matter] is so deeply hidden that it will not be recognized [or: made known], and that it will not come into the open [or: into disclosure].

translation_notes: כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because/that'. Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal clause explaining the preceding lamp analogy.

שום (SWM): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 same, H7762 'garlic'. In post-biblical Hebrew שום functions as 'any' (as in שום דבר = 'any thing/nothing'). Chose H7760 as the base form from which this indefinite usage derives.
דבר (DBR): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because שום דבר = 'any thing/matter' is the natural reading.
textual_notes: א#ינינו appears to be אינינו, a form of אין with a pronominal suffix ('it is not'). The # marker may indicate a textual note or uncertain letter.
ביות#ר appears to be ביותר ('exceedingly/most'), a post-biblical Hebrew adverbial form. The # may indicate a textual uncertainty.

verses.literal: For any thing is not exceedingly hidden that not it will be recognized and that not it will come into the open

verses.translation: Therefore, see in what manner you are hearing, for to the one who has [something], [more] will be given [or: added], and the one who does not have — even what he thinks he has will be taken from him.

translation_notes: זה (ZH): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because it serves as a demonstrative modifying אופן — 'this manner'.
אופן (AWPN): H212 'a wheel'. In post-biblical Hebrew אופן means 'manner/way'. The consonants are identical. Chose H212 as the base entry, understanding the semantic development to 'manner'.
כי (KY): Chose H3588 as the conjunction 'for/because', introducing the explanation of why they should take care how they hear.
מה (MH): Candidates: H4100 'what/how'. Chose H4100 as the interrogative/relative pronoun functioning here as 'what [he thinks]'.
textual_notes: יעשוק — the consonants could derive from עשק (H6231 'to oppress/wrong') or could be a scribal form related to 'be added/given more'. In context of 'to the one who has, more will be given', the expected sense is 'will be added/given'. This may be a textual corruption or an unusual usage. The parallel at the end of section 9 shows both יעסוק and יעשוק, suggesting scribal uncertainty.
0חוש#ב — the leading 0 and internal # suggest textual damage or scribal marks. The consonants חשב point to 'think/reckon/consider'.
בא#י — appears to be באיזה or באי ('in what/which'), with # marking uncertain text.

verses.literal: Therefore see in what manner you [are] hearing for to that one that there is to him will be added and that one that there is not to him what he thinks that will be to him will be taken from him

verses.translation: And [there] came to Yeshua his mother and his brothers.

translation_notes: ואחיו: The candidate H283 is 'Achio' (a proper name). However, the consonants אחיו naturally parse as אח ('brother') + יו (3ms possessive suffix) = 'his brothers'. The context of 'his mother and his brothers' confirms this is not a proper name.

verses.literal: And came to Yeshua his mother and his brothers

verses.translation: And they said to him: Your mother and your brothers desire [or: wish, long] to see you.

textual_notes: חפ#צים — the # may indicate textual uncertainty in one consonant. The root חפצ means 'to delight in, desire, take pleasure in'. The plural participle form fits: 'desiring/wishing'.

verses.literal: And they said to him your mother and your brothers [are] desiring to see you

verses.translation: And he answered and said to them: My mother and my brothers — they are those who hear the word of YHWH and put it into practice [or: action, deed].

translation_notes: וענה ('NH): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 same as H6030, H6033 same as H6031, H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because 'he answered and said' is a standard Hebrew narrative formula.

ואמר (W'MR): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' paired with 'answered' is the standard formula.
להם (LHM): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', or ל + H1992 'to them'. Chose ל + H1992 because 'he said to them' is the natural syntax.
דבר (DBR): Chose H1697 'word/matter' because 'the word of YHWH' is the consistent phrase in this manuscript.
אמי: H532 is 'Ami' (a proper name). However, the consonants parse naturally as אם + י (1cs suffix) = 'my mother'. Context demands 'my mother'.
ואחי: H277/H278 are proper names. However, אח + י = 'my brothers'. Context demands 'my brothers'.
למעשה (LM'SH): Candidates: H4639 'deed/action/work', H6213 'to do/make'. Chose H4639 because the preposition ל + noun 'deed' gives 'into practice/action'.
textual_notes: ושמוהו — appears to be 'and they put it' (from שים, 'to put/place'), with a 3ms object suffix. This could also be read as 'and they kept/guarded it' if from שמר, but the consonants lack ר, so שים is the clear root.

verses.literal: And he answered and said to them my mother and my brothers they [are] those that hear [the] word [of] YHWH and put it to deed

verses.translation: And it happened on one of the days that Yeshua boarded [or: went up into] a certain ship, and his disciples [were] with him. And Yeshua said to them: Let us cross over to the other side of the river [or: waterway]. And they all boarded [or: went up into] the ship.

translation_notes: באחד ('HD): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'on one of the days' is a natural temporal expression.

עלה ('LH): Candidates: H5927 'to ascend/go up', H5928 'holocaust', H5929 'leaf', H5930 'burnt offering', H5931 'pretext'. Chose H5927 because boarding a ship is described as 'going up' — the standard Hebrew idiom for embarking.
אמר ('MR): Chose H559 'to say' for the same reasons as in section 7.
להם (LHM): Chose ל + H1992 'to them' as in previous sections.
textual_notes: ליאור — this appears to be ל + יאור ('to the river/Nile'). The word יאור (H2975) typically refers to the Nile or a large watercourse/channel. In context of crossing by ship, 'river' or 'waterway' fits well.
מ#ע#בר — the # marks suggest textual uncertainty. The consonants עבר point to 'crossing/other side' (H5676). With מ prefix: 'from the other side' or 'across'.
כ4לם — the numeral 4 within the word suggests a scribal mark or textual note. The intended reading appears to be כלם ('all of them').

verses.literal: And it happened on one [of] the days that Yeshua went up into a ship one and his disciples [were] with him and Yeshua said to them let us cross across to the river and went up all of them into the ship

verses.translation: And while they were sailing, Yeshua the Messiah [or: the Anointed One] was sleeping. And a great storm of wind came upon the river [or: waterway], so that the ship was filled with water and they were perishing.

translation_notes: וכאשר (WK'SR): Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר = 'when/as' is the standard temporal conjunction.
משיח (MSYH): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'shrub'. Chose H4899 because 'Yeshua Messiah' identifies the sleeping figure by his title.
היה (HYH): Candidates: H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'was sleeping' requires the auxiliary verb 'was'.

מים (MYM): Candidates: H4325 'water', H3220 'sea', H3221 same, H3222 'warm spring'. Chose H4325 because the ship filling with 'water' during a storm is the natural image. The ים here is the intensifying form — 'fullness of water' — confirmed by the singular concept.
גדולה (GDWLH): H1420 'greatness/mighty acts'. This serves as the feminine adjective 'great' modifying the feminine noun סערה ('storm').
textual_notes: The remainder of section 9 after ואובדים appears to be heavily corrupted scribal notes or draft marginalia rather than continuous narrative text. Words like שיניחו, שיניחהו, באופןשהיה, repeated באופן שיהיה, and fragments like ן, ו, מתעשקין, יעסוק, יעשוק appear to be scribal repetitions from other sections (sections 2, 3, 4) — possibly catch-words, corrections, or variant readings that were inadvertently incorporated into the text. I have translated only the coherent narrative portion and flag the remainder as corrupt.
ביאור — same as section 8's ליאור; this is ב + יאור ('on/in the river').
שהאוניה — ש + ה + אוניה: 'that the ship'. אוניה is a post-biblical Hebrew word for 'ship' related to אניה (H591).
נתמל#את — the # suggests textual uncertainty. The root מלא ('to fill') in a reflexive/passive form: 'was filled'.
יש#ן — the # suggests textual uncertainty. The root ישן means 'to sleep' (H3462).

verses.literal: And when they [were] sailing Yeshua Messiah was sleeping and came a storm great of wind on the river that the ship was filled [with] water and [they were] perishing

verses.translation: And they drew near to Yeshua and woke him, and said: Master [or: Rabbi], behold, we are perishing! And Yeshua rose and commanded the wind and the storm [or: tempest] to stop [or: stand still]. And it stopped, and a great calm [or: stillness, rest] came about.

translation_notes: אל ('L) — first instance: Candidates: H408 'not', H409 same, H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H412 same, H413 'to/near'. Chose H413 because 'they approached to Yeshua' requires the directional preposition.
הנה (HNH): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'behold, we are perishing!' is a natural exclamation of distress.
אל ('L) — second instance: Chose H413 'to' because 'he commanded to the wind' directs the command toward its object.

הרוח (HRWH): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/deliverance', H7306 'to smell', H7307 'wind/spirit/breath', H7308 same. Chose H7307 because commanding 'the wind' during a storm is the coherent physical image.
והסער (WHSA'R): Candidates: H5590 'to rush upon/toss', H5591 'hurricane/storm'. Chose H5591 because it functions as the noun 'the storm' paired with 'the wind' as objects of the command.

ועמד (W'MD): Candidates: H5975 'to stand', H5976 'to shake', H5977 'a spot', H5978 'along with'. Chose H5975 because 'to stand' = 'to stop/be still' is the natural response to the command — the wind and storm ceased.

נחת (NHT): Candidates: H5181 'to sink/descend', H5182 same, H5183 'rest/quietness', H5184 'Nachath (name)', H5185 'descending'. Chose H5183 because 'a great calm/rest' describes the result of the storm ceasing — a coherent physical image of tranquility on the water.
גדול (GDWL): H1419 'great'. Note: נחת is typically feminine, but the adjective here is masculine גדול. This may reflect the late Hebrew style of this manuscript or treat נחת as masculine.
textual_notes: קם — root קום (H6965 'to rise'). Parsed as 3ms perfect: 'he rose/stood up'. No ambiguity.
The grammatical gender mismatch between נחת (usually feminine) and גדול (masculine) may indicate that this text treats נחת as masculine, or it may reflect a scribal preference.

verses.literal: And they approached to Yeshua and they woke him and said Master behold we [are] perishing and Yeshua rose and commanded to the wind and the storm to stand and it stood and there was made a calm great

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to them, Where is your faith? And they feared [with] a great fear, and they saw and were astonished, and said, Who is this one, that to the wind [or: spirit] and to the sea he says Stand still — and they obey him?

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because this is a narrative speech introduction — Yeshua 'said' to them.
להם: The prefix ל + הם. H1992 'them' fits as the indirect object of 'said'; H3859 'to rankle' makes no sense here.

אנה (consonants אנה): Candidates: H578 'to groan', H579 'to approach/meet'. Neither directly means 'where,' but אנה is well-attested as an interrogative adverb 'where' in Hebrew (cf. Gen 16:8). Chose interrogative 'where' because the sentence asks about the location/existence of their faith.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as a copula 'is' — 'where is your faith.'

וי ר או: These fragments appear to be a broken/damaged form of וייראו 'and they feared.' The וי is the narrative prefix, ר and או together reconstruct יראו. This is confirmed by the following noun יראה גדולה 'great fear.'
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep'. Chose H2088 because 'who is he, this one' is coherent; 'who is he, a sheep' is not.
רוח (consonants רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7307 'wind/spirit'. Chose H7307 because the context describes commanding natural elements — wind and sea.
ולים: ו + ל + ים. H3220 'sea' fits perfectly alongside 'wind' in a storm-calming narrative.
אומר: While H201 'Omar' is listed, the consonants אומר clearly function as a participle of אמר 'saying/says' (active participle). Chose H559 participial form.
textual_notes: The fragments וי / ר / או appear to be a single word וייראו ('and they feared') that was broken in transmission. The reconstruction is strongly supported by the cognate accusative יראה גדולה that follows.

אנה as 'where' is not listed among the Strong's candidates provided (H578 'groan', H579 'approach'), but the interrogative use of אנה is well-attested in Biblical Hebrew. This may reflect a gap in the provided candidate list.
אמונתכם has no Strong's candidates listed; it is clearly אמונה 'faith/faithfulness' + כם 'your (plural)' suffix.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said to them where is your faith and they feared [a] fear great and they saw and they marveled and said who is he this that to [the] wind and to [the] sea says stand and they obey him

verses.translation: And they came and crossed over to the region of Genisar, that which [is] near [or: adjacent] to the Galilee [district].

translation_notes: אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Chose H413 because the context describes movement toward a destination.

מלכות (consonants מלכות): Candidates: H4438 'dominion/rule/region'. In this context it denotes a governed territory or region — the district of Genisar. The reading as כות (H3575 'Cuth') is unlikely as it would leave מל unexplained.
textual_notes: מלכות here seems to be used in the sense of a governed region or district rather than 'kingdom' in its grandest sense. This is a common extended usage.
ובאו: The provided candidate H176 'or' applies only to the root או; the form here is clearly ו + באו (and they came), from בוא 'to come/enter'.
גניסר is a proper place name (Gennesaret) with no Strong's entry provided.

verses.literal: And they came and they crossed over to [the] region [of] Genisar that which [is] adjacent to the Galilee

verses.translation: And when they went out onto the land, there came to Yeshua a certain man whom a demon [or: malignant spirit] had seized [for] a long time, and he was not wearing any clothing, and he was not dwelling in a house — only among the tombs.

translation_notes: אשר (in וכאשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 — כאשר is a standard temporal conjunction 'when'.
אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 because context describes an individual man approaching Yeshua.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one man' = 'a certain man'.

שד (consonants שד): Candidates: H7699 'breast', H7700 'a demon', H7701 'violence/ravage'. Chose H7700 because the narrative describes a person seized by a malignant entity, which aligns with 'demon.' A breast or violence would not 'seize' a person in this syntactic construction.
זה (consonants זה): H2088 'this/that' chosen as demonstrative — 'this [was a] time much' = for a long time. H2089 'sheep' makes no sense here.
זמן (consonants זמן): Candidates: H2163 'to fix a time', H2165 'an appointed occasion/time'. Chose H2165 as the noun 'time' — 'a long time.'
רב (consonants רב): Candidates: H7227 'abundant/much', H7228 'archer'. Chose H7227 — 'much time' = a long time.
שום (consonants שום): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7762 'garlic'. H7760 in later Hebrew usage functions as 'any' (שום דבר = anything). Chose H7760 in this adjectival/indefinite sense.
מלבוש (consonants מלבוש): Candidates: H4403 'garment/clothing', H3830 'garment', H954 'to be ashamed'. Chose H4403 as the full form with מ prefix — 'clothing.'
בבית (consonants בבית): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1006 'Bajith'. Chose H1004 — 'in a house' is the natural reading.
רק (consonants רק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 — 'only in tombs' provides the logical contrast.
textual_notes: ואינינו appears to be a later Hebrew/Aramaic negation form (אין + suffix 'he is not'). No Strong's candidates were provided; it functions as a negating copula.
בקברים: No candidates listed. From root קבר 'grave/tomb' with plural suffix and prefix ב 'in'.

verses.literal: And when they went out on [the] land came to Yeshua [a] man one that seized him [a] demon this [was a] time much and he was not wearing any garment and he was not staying in [a] house only in tombs

verses.translation: And when he saw Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah], he fell before him, crying out in a great [or: loud] voice and said, What [is it] to you, Yeshua, to come to me? Son of the God most high [or: the Supreme Mighty One], I am seeking [or: begging] from you that you not torment me!

translation_notes: ראה (consonants ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7203 'seer/vision'. Chose H7200 — narrative describes the man seeing Yeshua and reacting.

משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7880 'shrubbery'. Chose H4899 — the text identifies Yeshua with a title; 'anointed one' fits as an appositional title. 'Shrubbery' or 'pondering' would be incoherent here.
נפל (consonants נפל): Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5309 'an abortion'. Chose H5307 — 'he fell before him' is a natural prostration gesture.
אמר (in ואמר): Chose H559 'to say' — speech introduction.
מה (consonants מה): H4100 'what?' — interrogative exclamation: 'what [is there between] you and me?'
האל (consonants האל with ה prefix): Candidates: H410 'God/mighty', H408 'not'. Chose H410 with definite article — 'the God' fits 'son of the God Most High.'
מאד (consonants מאד): H3966 'vehemently/exceedingly' vs H108 'fog'. Chose H3966 — modifies 'Most High' intensively.
עליון (consonants עליון): H5945 'the Supreme/Most High'. Fits the divine epithet 'God Most High.'
מבקש (consonants מבקש): H1245 'to search out/seek/request' vs H7179 'straw'. Chose H1245 — 'I am seeking/requesting from you' is coherent; 'straw' is not.
אני (consonants אני): H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship'. Chose H589 — first person pronoun in a plea.
textual_notes: מאד עליון: The phrase could be read as 'the exceedingly Most High God' (מאד intensifying עליון) or as two separate modifiers of אל. The overall meaning is clear: supreme divine being.
תצערני: No Strong's candidates provided. The root צער means 'to cause pain/torment' in later Hebrew. The form is 2ms imperfect + 1cs suffix: 'you torment me.'
לבא אלי: Could be parsed as 'to come to me' (infinitive of בוא + preposition אל + suffix) — the demon is asking why Yeshua has come to him.

verses.literal: And when he saw Yeshua [the] Anointed [one] he fell before him crying out in [a] voice great and said what to you Yeshua to come to me son of the God exceedingly Most High seeking I from you that not you torment me

verses.translation: For he had been commanding the evil [or: harmful] spirit to go out from that man — and it was tormenting Yeshua [with resistance] — and [he said] to the storm, Stand still! And they stood. She [the spirit] would [... text unclear ...] and he had been bound with iron chains and with cords, and when the bonds were broken, he was driven into the wilderness by the power of the demons.

translation_notes: כי (consonants כי): H3588 'because/for' vs H3587 'a brand'. Chose H3588 — explanatory conjunction introducing a reason.
רוח (in לרוח): Chose H7307 'spirit' — the entity possessing the man is called a spirit, not wind here.

רעה (consonants רעה): Candidates: H7462 'to tend a flock', H7463 'companion', H7465 'breakage/evil'. Chose H7465 — 'evil spirit' is coherent; 'shepherding spirit' or 'companion spirit' are not natural in context of demonic possession.
מן (consonants מן): H4480 'from/out of' — 'go out from the man.' H4478 'manna' and H4482 'musical chord' make no sense.
האדם (consonants האדם with ה prefix): H120 'human being' — 'the man' with definite article. The man previously introduced.
ההוא (consonants ההוא): H1931 'that one' with definite article — 'that man.'
והיה (consonants והיה): H1961 'to be/become' — 'and he was/had been.' H1962 'ruin' does not fit as a verb here.
במדבר (consonants במדבר): H4057 'wilderness/desert' — the man was driven into the desert. The alternative readings (speech, pestilence) do not fit being physically led somewhere.
בכח (consonants בכח): H3581 'power/force' — 'by the power of the demons.'
textual_notes: ר׳ appears to be an abbreviation, possibly for רבנו ('our master') or another title. The text is unclear here.

ואלהסערה: This appears to be a compound — ואל + הסערה 'and to the storm.' The ה is the definite article, and סערה means 'storm/tempest.' This seems to be a parenthetical reference back to the storm-calming episode.
The fragments ויל / ר / או are severely damaged or abbreviated text. They may reconstruct to a phrase about the spirit's actions but cannot be confidently translated.
ה דים (separated): This appears to be השדים 'the demons' with the ש dropped or separated in transmission. The same pattern appears in sections 7, 8, 9.

ומצערו לישוע: The syntax is ambiguous — it could mean 'and it was tormenting him' (the demon tormenting the man) or 'and [the man] was tormenting Yeshua [with his resistance/behavior].' The former reading is more natural in context.

verses.literal: For in his commanding to [the] spirit evil that it go out from the man that and it was tormenting Yeshua [... unclear] and to the storm that they stand and they stood she and [... unclear ...] and he was bound in chains [of] iron and in cords and when the bonds were broken he was led into [the] wilderness by [the] power of the demons

verses.translation: And Yeshua asked him, What [is] your name? And he answered him, Legion [or: Number/Multitude], for many demons had entered into him.

translation_notes: מה (consonants מה): H4100 'what?' — interrogative asking for the name.
והוא (consonants והוא): H1931 'he' — subject pronoun for the response.

מספר (consonants מספר): Candidates: H4557 'a number/multitude', H5608 'to inscribe/recount', H5612 'a book'. Chose H4557 — the demon gives its name as 'Number/Multitude,' equivalent to the concept of 'Legion' (many). This is confirmed by the explanatory clause 'for many demons entered into him.'
כי (consonants כי): H3588 'for/because' — explanatory conjunction.
שדים: While H7708 'Siddim' (a valley) is the listed candidate, the consonants שדים are clearly the plural of שד H7700 'demon.' The text explicitly speaks of many demons entering the man.
textual_notes: מך: No candidates provided. This appears to be שמך 'your name' with the ש elided or absorbed into the preceding word (the ש of שאלו). The full reading would be: מה שמך 'what [is] your name?'
שאלו: The provided candidates (H431 'lo!', H432 'if') apply only to אלו. The form is clearly שאל + ו suffix = 'asked him', from the root שאל 'to ask.'
מספר as the demon's name: This Hebrew word 'Number' appears to be translating the concept rendered elsewhere as 'Legion' — a name signifying multitude.

verses.literal: And Yeshua asked him what [is your] name and he answered him Number for demons many entered in him

verses.translation: And the demons pleaded [with] Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah] that he not command them to go into the abysses [or: the depths].

translation_notes: משיח (consonants משיח): H4899 'anointed/Messiah' vs H7880 'shrubbery'. Chose H4899 — title of Yeshua, consistent with section 4.
שלא: ש (that) + לא H3808 (not) = 'that not.'
וה דים: Same pattern as section 5 — השדים 'the demons' with ש separated.
textual_notes: בתהומות: No candidates provided. From תהום 'the deep/abyss' (cf. H8415) with plural suffix and prefix ב. The demons plead not to be sent into the primordial depths.
יצוה: No candidates provided. This is the 3ms jussive/imperfect of צוה 'to command' — 'that he not command them.'

verses.literal: And the demons sought Yeshua [the] Anointed [One] that not he command them that they go into [the] abysses

verses.translation: And there were there [pigs] grazing on the mountain, and the demons entreated [the] face of Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah] that he give them permission to enter into [the pigs], those ones. And so he did.

translation_notes: שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name'. Chose H8033 — 'there were there pigs' = pigs were present at that location.
בהר: ב + הר H2022 'mountain' — 'on the mountain' where pigs were grazing.
להם: ל + הם H1992 'them' — indirect object 'give to them.'
ההם: ה + הם H1992 — demonstrative 'those' modifying the pigs.
כן (in וכן): H3651 'so/thus' — 'and so he did.'
עשה (consonants עשה): H6213 'to do/make' — 'he did [it].'
משיח: H4899 'anointed/Messiah' — consistent title throughout.
textual_notes: חלו פני: The root חלה means 'to be sick' or 'to entreat the face of' (to make supplication). Here it clearly means 'entreated/implored' — they sought favor from Yeshua.
]חזירים[: The brackets in the source text indicate this word was likely marked by a scribe as uncertain or inserted. חזיר means 'pig/swine.'
בקרבי: ב + קרב 'midst/interior' + suffix. 'In the midst/interior of' = 'into the bodies of' the pigs.

לשלום (H7965/H7966/H7967): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/wholeness', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'go to peace/wholeness' is a coherent blessing formula, while 'go to a fee' or 'go to Shallum' makes no contextual sense.

לכי: The candidate listed is כי (H3588 'because/that'), but with the prefix ל this would be 'for because' which is awkward. This is clearly the feminine imperative of הלך 'to go' — 'go!' — addressed to the woman. No Strong's entry for הלך was provided in the candidates.

verses.literal: And-[a] chief-of [the] house-of the-assembly came to-him and-said to-him do-not desire to-trouble Yeshua [the] Anointed for your-daughter [has] died
verses.amplified: And [a] leader [or: ruler, head person] of the house of the assembly [synagogue] came to him and said to him: Do not wish to trouble [or: distress] Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah], for your daughter has died.
work: שר (H8269/H8270): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/ruler', H8270 'a string/umbilical cord'. Chose H8269 because 'a ruler of the house of the assembly' describes a synagogue official, while 'a string of the house' is incoherent.
בית (H1004/H1006): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1006 'Bajith (place)'. Chose H1004 because 'house of the assembly' (synagogue) is a known institutional term.

אל (H408/H410/H413): Chose H408 'not' (deprecative negation) because it precedes an imperfect verb תחפוץ forming the prohibitive 'do not desire/wish.' H413 'to' and H410 'God' do not fit before a verb of wanting.

לצער (H6819/H6820): Candidates: H6819 'to be small/ignoble' (figuratively: to trouble, distress), H6820 'Tsoar (place name)'. Chose H6819 because 'do not wish to trouble/distress' the teacher makes narrative sense — someone tells the father not to bother Yeshua further. 'Do not wish to Tsoar' is nonsensical.
ואמר (H559/H561/H563): Chose H559 'to say' — the narrative verb. Same reasoning as section 2.
כי (H3587/H3588): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Chose H3588 because 'for your daughter has died' provides the causal explanation.

בתך: The candidate listed is H8496 תך 'oppression,' but with ב prefix that would mean 'in oppression' which does not fit. The consonants בתך naturally read as בת + ך 'your daughter' (בת H1323 'daughter' + 2ms suffix). This is the contextually obvious reading.
ambiguities: הכנסת: No Strong's candidate was provided. This is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'assembly/synagogue' (כנסת from the root כנס 'to gather'). It is a known term in later Hebrew texts.
בתך: Could theoretically be parsed as ב + תך (H8496 'in oppression'), but the narrative context — a father being told his daughter has died — overwhelmingly supports 'your daughter.'

verses.literal: And-Yeshua heard this and-said to-[the]-father-of the-girl do-not fear trust in-YHWH and-believe and-she-will-be saved
verses.amplified: And Yeshua heard this and said to the father of the girl: Do not be afraid — trust [or: be confident] in YHWH, and believe, and she will be delivered [saved, rescued].
work: שמע (H8085-H8090): Candidates include 'to hear intelligently' (H8085), 'something heard/report' (H8088/H8089), and place/personal names. Chose H8085 because the narrative requires the verb 'he heard' — Yeshua heard the news about the daughter's death.

זה (H2088/H2089/H2090): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose H2088 because 'he heard this' (referring to the preceding speech) is coherent, while 'he heard a sheep' is bizarre in context.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard narrative verb.

לאבי: The candidate H21 is 'Abi' (a personal name), but in context לאבי reads as ל + אבי 'to the father of' (from אב H1 'father' in construct with suffix). 'To the father of the girl' fits the narrative perfectly.
הנערה (H5291/H5292): Candidates: H5291 'a girl (infancy to adolescence)', H5292 'Naarah (name/place)'. Chose H5291 because 'the girl' with the definite article refers to the daughter just mentioned.
אל (H408/H410/H413): Chose H408 'do not' because it precedes the imperfect תפחד forming a prohibitive command: 'do not fear.'

בטח (H982/H983/H984): Candidates: H982 'to trust/be confident', H983 'safety/security', H984 'Betach (place)'. Chose H982 because the imperative 'trust in YHWH' fits the exhortation context, whereas 'safety in YHWH' would need different syntax.
ביהוה (H3068/H3069): Both refer to the divine name YHWH. Chose H3068 as the standard entry.
ambiguities: לאבי: Could be read as the proper name Abi (H21) with prefix ל, but context strongly favors 'to the father of' — a construct phrase with the following noun הנערה.

ותהי נושעת: This could be parsed as 'and she will be saved/delivered' (future/jussive of היה + passive participle of ישע), or potentially 'and let her be saved' (cohortative sense). The jussive/future reading fits the promise-like tone of Yeshua's words.

verses.translation: And when Yeshua came into the house of the chief [or: ruler], he did not permit [or: allow] any person to enter with him.

translation_notes: וכשבא: Listed candidate H7614 'Sheba (name)' for שבא. However, the consonants וכשבא naturally parse as ו + כ (when) + ש (relative/conjunction) + בא (came, from בוא). 'And when he came' is the only coherent reading.
בבית (consonants ב-ב-י-ת): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1006 'Bajith.' Chose H1004 with prefix ב = 'in the house of.'
השר (consonants ה-ש-ר): Candidates: H8269 'chief/head person', H8270 'string/cord.' Chose H8269 because 'the house of the chief' continues the synagogue ruler narrative.
עזב (consonants ע-ז-ב): H5800 'to loosen, relinquish, permit.' Here used in the sense of 'permit/allow' — 'he did not permit any person to enter.'
לשום (consonants ל-ש-ו-ם): Candidates: H7760 'to put/set', H7762 'garlic.' However, in context לשום functions as 'to any' (ל + שום in the sense of 'any/some'), a common usage in post-biblical Hebrew.
אדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates: H120 'human being', H121 'Adam (name)', H123 'Edom.' Chose H120 because 'any person' fits the context of restricting entry.
textual_notes: שיכנס uses the root כנס 'to gather/enter' with Aramaic-influenced prefix ש as relative — another indicator of post-biblical Hebrew or Aramaic substrate in this manuscript.
עזב meaning 'permit/allow' is an extension of its basic meaning 'to leave/let go' — context here demands the permissive sense rather than 'abandon.'

verses.literal: And when Yeshua came in [the] house [of] the chief he did not permit to any person that he enter with him

verses.translation: [They were] weeping [for] the girl, and Yeshua said to them: Do not weep, for the girl is not dead — [she is] only sleeping. He sent his messengers [or: emissaries] before him, and they entered into [a] city of the Samaritans to prepare [things] there.

translation_notes: הנערה (both occurrences): Candidates: H5291 'a girl (infancy to adolescence)', H5292 'Naarah (proper name/place)'. In context of weeping for a dead person and Yeshua saying 'the girl is not dead,' H5291 'the girl' is the clear reading.
אמר: H559 'to say' — Yeshua as subject.
אל: H408 'do not' — negative imperative before תבכו 'weep.'
כי: H3588 'for/because' — introducing the reason not to weep.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. As negation of the nominal clause 'the girl is dead,' H369 'is not' is correct.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. As an adverb contrasting 'not dead' with 'sleeping,' H7535 'only/merely' is the clear reading.

שלח: Candidates: H7971 'to send away/out', H7972 same, H7973 'spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach (name)', H7975 'Shiloach (fountain)', H3892 'fresh', H3893 'freshness'. As a verb with שלוחיו 'his messengers' as object, 'he sent' (H7971) is the only coherent reading.

בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'a watcher/angel', H5895 'a young ass'. With ה<ומרונים (Samaritans) following, 'in the city of' (H5892) is the correct reading.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name'. As an adverb at the end of 'to prepare ___,' 'there' (H8033) is the natural reading.
textual_notes: This section appears to combine material from two different episodes: (1) Yeshua saying the girl is not dead but sleeping, and (2) sending messengers to a Samaritan city. This may be a textual juxtaposition or the manuscript may be preserving a connected narrative sequence.
לה״ם has a scribal mark (״) that may indicate abbreviation or damage. Reading as להם 'to them' is straightforward.
ה<ומרונים contains a scribal mark (<). The expected reading is השומרונים 'the Samaritans' — the < likely represents a damaged or uncertain letter (ש).

verses.translation: And [they were] ridiculing Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah] when he said this — [and they did not receive him] — because the set purpose [or: intent, direction] of his face [was toward] Jerusalem

translation_notes: על (consonants ע-ל): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/against', H5923 'yoke'. In context of mocking directed at a person, H5921 'against/upon' is the natural preposition.

משיח (consonants מ-ש-י-ח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'ponder/converse', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'shrubbery'. Following a proper name (Yeshua), this is clearly a title — H4899 'anointed one/Messiah' fits as an apposition to Yeshua.
כי (consonants כ-י): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Context requires a causal conjunction explaining why they didn't receive him — H3588.
textual_notes: ז״ה appears to be an abbreviation with gershayim marks, likely standing for 'this' (זה). The brackets around ולא קבלוהו suggest an editorial insertion or marginal gloss in the manuscript.
מגמת is not in the candidate list but contextually reads as a construct form meaning 'direction/purpose of' — a relatively rare word in biblical Hebrew.

verses.translation: And Yeshua the Anointed One took the girl by his hand and said 'Arise!' And when Yaaqov [Jacob] and Yochanan [John] saw [this] they said 'Master [or: Lord], do you wish [or: desire] that we command fire [to] descend from the heavens [or: the sky] and consume them all?'

translation_notes: לקח (consonants ל-ק-ח): Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. Context describes a physical action with a girl — H3947 'took' is coherent; 'instruction' does not fit.

הנערה (consonants נ-ע-ר-ה): Candidates: H5291 'a girl', H5292 'Naarah (proper name)'. With the definite article ה and the narrative of taking by hand and commanding 'arise (feminine)', H5291 'the girl' is clearly correct.
ואמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Context requires a verb of speech — H559.
אדון (consonants א-ד-ו-ן): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Used as a form of address before a question — H113 'lord/master'.
חפץ (consonants ח-פ-ץ): Candidates: H2654 'to be pleased/to desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. As a verb before אתה, H2654 functions as 'do you desire?' — a direct question.
אתה (consonants א-ת-ה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Following חפץ, the pronoun 'you' (H859) makes sense as the subject of the question.
ירד (consonants י-ר-ד): Candidates: H3381 'to descend', H3382 'Jered (name)'. Context of fire coming down from heavens — H3381 'descend'.
אש (consonants א-ש): Candidates: H784 'fire', H786 'there is', H787 'foundation'. Fire descending from heavens is a coherent image — H784.
מן (consonants מ-ן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4480 'from/out of'. Preposition 'from' before 'the heavens' — H4480.
את (consonants א-ת): Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with', H855 'hoe'. Before כולם as the object of burning — H853 direct object marker.
textual_notes: ה<מים has a damaged/unclear consonant marked with <. The context (fire descending from ___) strongly suggests השמים 'the heavens/sky'. The missing consonant is likely ש.
בידו: The candidate H3035 'Jiddo (proper name)' does not fit; this is clearly ב + יד + ו 'in his hand' with pronominal suffix.

שנאמר could be parsed as ש + נאמר 'that we say/command' (1st person plural imperfect with relative prefix ש), or ש + נאמר 'that it was said' (niphal). The active first-person reading fits the context of the disciples asking permission.

verses.translation: And the breath [or: spirit, life-force] returned to her and immediately she stood up. And Yeshua commanded that they give her [something] to eat. Then Yeshua turned and said to them 'You do not know from what manner of spirit you [are].'

translation_notes: והרוח (consonants ר-ו-ח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely/revive', H7305 'room', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'wind/spirit (Aramaic)'. The subject that 'returned in her' — H7307 'spirit/breath/life' is the coherent reading: her life-breath returned.
להם (consonants ל-ה-ם): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. As a prepositional phrase ל + הם 'to them' after 'said' — clearly the pronoun H1992.

מאי (consonants מ-א-י): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Combined with following זה, 'from what' (מ + אי) functions as an interrogative — H335 'where/what'.
זה (consonants ז-ה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. As a demonstrative modifying רוח, H2088 'this/that' creates 'what manner of spirit this [is]'.
רוח (second occurrence): Same candidates as above. Here used as 'spirit' in the sense of disposition or animating force — H7307.
textual_notes: ש״ appears to be an abbreviation (with gershayim) for the relative particle ש 'that'. ל״א+כול appears to be an abbreviated/scribal form for לאכול 'to eat'.
חזר is not among provided candidates — it is a post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew verb meaning 'returned'. This may indicate the manuscript's late linguistic register.

אתם: The only candidate H864 'Etham (place name)' does not fit; this is clearly the 2nd person plural pronoun 'you' (standard Hebrew אתם), which should map to a pronoun entry not provided in the candidate list.
ומיד could be parsed as ו + מיד 'and immediately' (adverbial use of 'from hand') or ו + מ + יד 'and from [the] hand'. The adverbial sense is standard in later Hebrew and fits the narrative flow.

verses.literal: And the spirit returned in her and immediately she arose and Yeshua commanded that they give to her to eat and turned Yeshua and said to them you do not know from what spirit you [are]

verses.translation: And her father and her mother were astonished [or: trembled]. And Yeshua the Anointed One commanded them not to tell anyone [about] what had been done. [For] the Son of Man did not come to destroy souls [or: lives] but rather to save them. And they departed from there and traveled to another village [or: town].

translation_notes: ואמה (consonants א-מ-ה): Candidates: H519 'maidservant', H520 'cubit/mother-unit', H522 'Ammah (place)'. Following 'and her father' — the parallel demands 'and her mother'. The consonants אמה with possessive suffix ה can be read as אמה 'her mother' (from אם with feminine suffix). H519 'maidservant' would be awkward after 'her father'; the natural pairing is father and mother.

וצום: The candidate list offers H6684 'to fast' and H6685 'a fast' for צום. However, in context this reads as ו + צו + ם = 'and commanded them' (from צוה with 3mp suffix). The form ויצום would be more standard, but this manuscript appears to use abbreviated/later forms. The fasting reading makes no contextual sense here — Yeshua is giving them an instruction.
אדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates include H119-H124. As 'any man/person' — H120 'human being' fits.
בן (consonants ב-ן): Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son'. In 'son of the man' — H1121.
האדם (consonants א-ד-ם with ה): H120 'human being' with definite article. 'The man/humanity' — forming the title 'Son of Man'.
לא (consonants ל-א): H3808 'not' — standard negation before 'came'.
לאבד (consonants א-ב-ד): Candidates: H6 'to perish/destroy', H7 (Aramaic same), H8 'destruction'. With ל prefix as infinitive 'to destroy' — H6.

אלא: H414 'Ela (name)' is the only candidate, but contextually this is clearly the conjunction אלא 'but rather' — a standard Mishnaic/post-biblical Hebrew conjunction not in the Strong's biblical lexicon.

במגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol (place in Egypt)', H1419 'great'. The word מגדול can also mean 'tower/fortified place' and by extension 'village/town'. With ב prefix and אחר 'another' following, 'in another village/town' is the natural reading.
אחר (consonants א-ח-ר): Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after', H312 'other/another'. Modifying 'village' — H312 'another' is correct.
textual_notes: ואביה: The candidate H29 'Abijah (proper name)' shares these consonants, but in context (paired with 'and her mother'), this is clearly אב + י + ה 'her father' with conjunction ו.
וצום is ambiguous between 'and commanded them' (from צוה) and 'and fasted' (from צום H6684). The following clause 'that they not tell' requires a verb of commanding, not fasting.
ש״לא, א״ת, ה״עשוי all contain abbreviation marks (gershayim ״), indicating scribal shorthand. ש״לא = שלא 'that not'; א״ת = את (object marker); ה״עשוי = העשוי 'what was done'.
לשץ ם is unclear — possibly a damaged or abbreviated form. It likely represents לשום אדם 'to any man' or a similar phrase. The ץ may be a scribal error or abbreviation.
The brackets ] [ in the text appear to indicate a lacuna or editorial gap in the manuscript.
מ<ם has a damaged consonant (<); likely משם 'from there'.

במגדול could be read as 'in Migdol' (the Egyptian place name H4024) or as 'in a tower/village'. Given the narrative of traveling to 'another' location, a generic 'village/town' reading is more coherent than a specific Egyptian location.
